### [Introducing Claude for Nonprofits](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-for-nonprofits)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-03

Anthropic has launched Claude for Nonprofits, offering eligible organizations up to 75% off Team and Enterprise plans, new open-source software connectors, and a free AI training course.

- Discounted access applies to Team and Enterprise plans, providing access to Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Haiku 4.5 models.
- Introduces three new open-source connectors for specialized nonprofit tools: Blackbaud, Candid, and Benevity.
- Integrates with existing platform connectors including Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Asana, Slack, and Box.
- Launches 'AI Fluency for Nonprofits', a free non-technical training course on Anthropic Academy created with GivingTuesday for workflows like grant writing and program evaluation.

**Why it matters:** This initiative significantly lowers the financial and technical barriers for non-profit organizations to integrate advanced AI models and specialized data connectors into their operational workflows.

### [Quoting Steve Yegge](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/4/steve-yegge/#atom-everything)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-08-04

Steve Yegge's AI agent project 'Gas Town' failed to remain functional after the release of Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7.

- Gas Town was built primarily to construct itself and functioned effectively using models up through Opus 4.6.
- Opus 4.7 introduced a 'just two more things' behavioral tic, causing the model to continuously refactor Gas Town rather than complete task convergence.
- The persistent loop behavior under Opus 4.7 ultimately led to the collapse and abandonment of Gas Town.

**Why it matters:** Model behavior shifts between minor LLM version updates can unexpectedly break complex recursive software development agents.
